Weight Degree Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch66.R
centrality_wdc.Rd

Weight degree centrality (Wdc; Liu et al. 2016) multiplies the number of non-backtracking two-step walks from a node by a power of its degree: $$Wdc(i) = \Bigl(\sum_{j \in N(i)} k_j - k_i\Bigr) k_i^{\alpha}, \qquad \alpha = |r|,$$ with \(k\) the degree and \(r\) the degree assortativity of the network.

Usage

centrality_wdc(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses wdc_alpha (the exponent, default NULL for the absolute degree assortativity).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. wdc_alpha = NULL, the default, takes \(\alpha = |r|\) as the source does; the source adds that other values can be used, and any single finite nonnegative number is accepted. The assortativity is 0/0 when every node with a tie has the same degree, on a regular network for instance; \(\alpha\) is then 0, the source's neutral case. With \(\alpha = 0\) the score is centrality_con on a simple undirected network, the number of common neighbors a node has with all the others together, and at the default it is that number times the degree to the power \(|r|\). The score ranks nodes much like centrality_con, centrality_expected and centrality_x_degree (Kendall correlation up to 0.994 on four test networks, 0.86 at the lowest). The source prints no value on a network available here, so the implementation is checked against the definition only. Isolated nodes score 0. A wdc_alpha that is negative or not finite raises a cograph_bad_parameter error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Liu, Y., Wei, B., Du, Y., Xiao, F. and Deng, Y. (2016). Identifying influential spreaders by weight degree centrality in complex networks. Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, 86, 1-7. doi:10.1016/j.chaos.2016.01.030 .

See also

centrality_ewdc, centrality_con, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_wdc(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   32.37679   39.97557   47.86470   38.43804   30.90512   33.84847   27.89810 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   36.79181   41.51309   36.79181 
centrality_wdc(regulation_net, wdc_alpha = 0)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>         22         26         30         25         21         23         20 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>         25         27         25
